visualReview.notes: Inspected the preview, four rotations and four detailed source views. The double verandah, paired doors, open upper balustrade, paired stairs, hooded metal windows and lower rear annex are visible. The main and annex roofs read as distinct volumes.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected nine shared viewer captures at the dated placement, including the four elevations, hood and balustrade detail, rear annex and overhead orientation. Plaster, masonry and the warm pitched roof read clearly. The unload check passed.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all twenty-five context, detail and transition images. The front porch and pitched roof persist throughout the four explicit detail levels. Near geometry exposes the balustrade openings, window hoods, pane divisions and roof seams.

geographicReview.notes: The named OpenStreetMap outline defines the rectangular two-unit plan with the southeast front projection and attached rear. Inspected the original terrain without a model cutout and the field-backed frontage. The rear plinth follows the rising slope in the preview. Finished grade and the stair-to-ground fit are estimates.

fidelityReview.scope: The existing two-storey Hung Lau in the February 2017 description, including the southeast verandah and attached two-storey rear kitchen and storeroom.
fidelityReview.notes: The February 2017 heritage appraisal describes a simple two-storey house with two units, faded pink plaster, a pitched roof, two-level verandah with pierced masonry, hooded metal windows and a rear kitchen and storeroom. The mapped outline defines the main volumes. Stair geometry, openings and plaster and roof color are architectural estimates.

imageryReview.notes: The cleared Qualla photographs document the grounds and memorial. The building is reconstructed from the 2017 written heritage appraisal and named native footprint, with no reference imagery used.

primaryFactsReview.notes: The 2017 heritage assessment and named native outline support the pitched two-storey house, southeast verandah with pierced masonry, and two-storey service annex. Section heights, the opening grid and local thresholds are estimates.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: February 2017 Red House (Hung Lau), with its southeast verandah and attached rear annex in Tuen Mun, Hong Kong.

limitations: The exterior follows the February 2017 heritage description and the twelve-point mapped outline. The map controls the house, verandah and rear projections.
Floor levels, roof pitch, window spacing, screen-block pattern and color are approximate interpretations of the written evidence.
The steep natural grade remains in its original source grid. Thresholds, footings and the short approach stairs use modeled elevations.
The reconstruction covers the standing house, verandah and attached service annex. The surrounding former farm is represented by the original terrain.
